title: jurassic-rampage · Wundur
author: YouCantGoThat_Way
selftext:
My 8-year-old has been directing the creation of a game called Jurassic Rampage using Unity: you play as a raptor in a tactical vest with a rifle, fighting zombies, rescuing survivors, and calling in a jet to extract. He decides what is fun or "boring," AI builds it, and I sit next to him to keep things from breaking.

Here is the pipeline we used:

* **Code (Claude Opus 5.5 + Unity 6):** Running inside Wundur (full disclosure: I have been building Wundur for him, a desktop app that wraps coding agents with game asset tools). My son asks for features in plain English ("make zombies faster when you rescue someone"), Claude writes the C# and WebGL build scripts, and he playtests immediately. That feedback loop is 90% of the process.
* **2D to 3D:** We generated 2D front, side, and back reference sheets first to fix proportions cheaply before touching 3D. He used a self hosted model to build the current playable raptor. He used Tripo and Meshy for some assets. gpt-image-2.5 for initial image building. ElevenLabs for sound effects.
* **Cleanup & Asset Store:** Nothing comes out game-ready. We rigged in Mixamo and claude wrote blender scripts to add tail bones, fix gun scaling, and unglue his tail from his legs. Zombies, town props, and the jet are cheap Unity Asset Store packs, which keeps the overall art style cohesive.

Biggest takeaway: 8-year-olds are ruthless playtesters, and fixing character designs in 2D turnarounds first saves a ton of time and 3D generation credits.

Someone recently reached level 10, and he hasn't stopped bragging about it. You can play it in your browser here: [https://jurassic-rampage-o7u8z8x0.wundur.games](https://jurassic-rampage-o7u8z8x0.wundur.games)

Happy to answer questions about the stack, or pass along feedback to my son if you try it out!

comments.body: W parent. Your child is lucky!
